data_point: Uses a fintech tool Puzzle connects to
run_when: Code found a mention of one of the tools but couldn't tell if the company itself uses it.

prompt.task: Decide whether the company itself uses at least one of: Mercury, Brex, Ramp, Stripe, Gusto, Rippling, Deel, Pulley, or Chase business banking.
prompt.definition: The company uses the tool for its own billing, payroll, banking, cards or cap table.
yes_when: Privacy policy or subprocessor list names the tool as a processor the company uses
Job posts say benefits or payroll run through Gusto, Rippling or Deel
The site says 'we bank with Mercury' or similar
no_when: Almost never provable. Use 'no' only if the text explicitly says they use a different tool instead and none of these
unknown_when: The tool is only named as an integration of their product
The tool is named as an investor or partner
watch_out_for: 'Connect your Stripe account' or 'integrates with Gusto' describes their product, not their own stack
Stripe or Brex listed among investors is not usage

evidence_quote.description: Exact words copied from the text. Empty when the answer is unknown.

source.description: Page name or URL the quote came from.

reason.description: One plain sentence explaining the answer.

tools_used.description: Only tools the company itself uses, proven by the quote.

queries: site:{domain} Stripe OR Gusto OR Rippling OR Deel OR Mercury OR Brex OR Ramp
"{company}" Stripe OR Gusto OR Rippling OR Mercury OR Brex OR Ramp OR Deel
good_sources: pages on the company's own domain

examples.input_excerpt: The payment processors we work with are: Stripe. Their privacy policy is at stripe.com/privacy

output.evidence_quote: The payment processors we work with are: Stripe
output.reason: The company names Stripe as its own payment processor.

examples.input_excerpt: Puzzle integrates with Stripe, Mercury, Brex and Gusto to pull in your transactions

output.reason: These are integrations of the product, not tools the company says it uses.
